name: Highlands 29

nadir.desc: The nadir view shows a single-story residence with a dark gray multi-pitch roof set back from a two-lane paved road that runs diagonally across the upper portion of the image|A curved driveway connects the property to the road, passing through a heavily vegetated parcel covered with dense juniper and scrub trees|A small area of irrigated green lawn is visible adjacent to the residence, and the surrounding terrain is arid sandy soil with scattered low desert vegetation|A paved cul-de-sac or loop road is visible to the right side of the image, suggesting a second road access point in the vicinity.

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the property from the road side, revealing a broad, open sandy approach with a curved paved driveway that arcs through the parcel toward the residence|Numerous juniper trees of varying height are distributed across the front of the property on both sides of the driveway, reducing sightlines to the structure from the road|The terrain between the road and the structure is relatively flat with scattered low desert shrubs|No gates, fencing, or other access control features are visible along the driveway approach from this perspective.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the right side of the property, with the curved driveway visible as it transitions from the road toward the residence in the background|The terrain on the right side is open sandy ground with scattered juniper trees of moderate density|The driveway curves through this side of the parcel and a small rock outcrop is visible near the mid-ground|Vegetation spacing on this side is sufficient to allow foot movement between trees, though the trees reduce direct sightlines across the parcel.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, which is dominated by dense juniper tree coverage with no visible cleared access routes or pathways along the rear perimeter|Rocky outcrops and sandy soil are visible beneath the tree canopy, and the terrain shows a gentle slope|No structures, fencing, gates, or utility features are visible from the rear perspective|Access to the rear of the property on foot would require navigation through closely spaced trees and uneven rocky ground.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property, which is densely covered with juniper trees across the full extent of the parcel edge|The terrain is sandy and relatively flat with no visible pathways, fencing, or cleared corridors along this side|Tree density on the left side is notably higher than on the right side, substantially limiting sightlines and foot movement|No structures or utility features are visible from this perspective.

considerations: Vehicle access to the residence is limited to a single curved paved driveway from the main two-lane road, with a secondary paved loop road visible to the east that does not appear to directly connect to this property's driveway. Dense juniper tree coverage on all sides of the structure significantly limits visibility of the residence from the road and restricts lateral movement around the building. The rear and left sides of the property have the heaviest tree density, making foot approach and egress in those directions difficult. Responders should anticipate limited staging space near the structure and restricted sightlines from the road to the front entrance.
clarifications: Does the curved driveway have sufficient width and surface load capacity to support the weight of fire apparatus or ambulances? Is there a secondary vehicle access point connecting the property to the cul-de-sac road visible to the east? Are there any gates or access controls on the driveway that would require a key, code, or manual override? Are there propane tanks, fuel storage, or other utility equipment located at the rear or sides of the structure that are not visible from the road? Is there a walkout or secondary exit on the rear or left side of the residence?
